dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Oh? Why, hello child.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: The flowers bloom and fade, people come and go, but the Lantern Rite will be held each year right on time.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: But this year's Rite is quite different from those of yesteryear. Go, go have a look around. Enjoy the sights and sounds of Liyue Harbor.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Adventure Challenge

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Duel

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Amazing. This is the game I've been thinking about for a long time...

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Don't underestimate me...

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Hmmm, I lost, young one. When it comes to cards, you seem to be the best at it.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Hehe, young one. You didn't let me win because of my age, did you?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: That's weird...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Granny, what's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two again. I was just sorting out my teapot.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: After you helped clean my teapot last time, I thought to myself, I really ought to give it a proper deep clean.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: It would make things so much easier when I wish to treat my guests to tea in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: So I took it down to the Bishui River and gave it a good old wash, inside and out. But it was no use. This teapot is so dreadfully difficult to clean.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Youngsters, would you help an old lady clean her teapot once more? For old time's sake?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave it to us.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Wonderful, thank you, youngsters.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry, I have other things to do.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Very well, never mind. You must have far more important things to attend to than helping an old lady with her spring cleaning.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is a beautiful flower.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Hehe, all thanks to the beautiful weather we're having today.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: I'd always hoped that one day this flower would bloom all over Liyue once more...

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: But in the meantime, would you take a few of these flowers from Yujing Terrace with you on your journey, so that they might see the world?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: ...The younger generation doesn't appreciate flowers anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Admiring the flowers?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: That I am. One season after the next, this flower blooms, then falls, only to bloom again. And on it goes — just like Liyue.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Look over here, and over here. So many flowers are blooming! It looks like this will be a blessed year.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What type of flowers are these?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: These are Glaze Lilies. Probably the last surviving ones in all of Liyue Harbor.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: People say that the sound of singing nourishes them, and helps them grow...

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: But the sound of fighting, of cursing... it is poison to them, and eats away at their roots.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: That is why, over centuries of strife, they have disappeared from Liyue's landscape.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Goodbye, young one. If you are ever passing by Jueyun Karst, please pass on my regards to my old friends.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: If it is meant to be that you see them... then you will see them.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Oh? Why, hello child.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Though flowers bloom yet always fade, but people go yet return another day. I just knew that you'd be back to see me before long, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about the past.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Just because my complexion screams "ancient history" doesn't mean I love discussing the past, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: ...Relax, I'm only kidding.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Truth be told, the older you get, the more time you have on your hands, and the more you start contemplating the past... I do wonder how my old friends back in the mountains are getting on...

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Liyue Harbor is really a wonderful place now. I wonder if they would ever want to step down into the mortal realm and get a taste of the lifestyle here...

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Look at me rambling on again, I must sound like a lunatic! Maybe one day I can discuss my past with you... if it is meant to be.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: This year's Mingxiao Lantern is dedicated to Skybracer... He always was a show off — I'm sure he'll be very pleased!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who's Skybracer?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: This year's Mingxiao Lantern will be the spitting image of him when it's complete!

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Well, that's the plan. I do hope they make the antlers big enough, they were his pride and joy after all.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: The story goes that the antlers were made from the very essence of Rex Lapis' divine power, which made it the hardest material in all of Liyue.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: But then, that fateful battle happened... The gods exchanged powerful blows, and the mountains started collapsing. To avoid impacting the villagers at the foot of the mountain, the adeptus got his friend to chop his antlers off...

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: He used those blood-drenched antlers as a wedge to prop up the mountain. And if that wasn't enough of a sacrifice, he then kept on fighting until his blood was drained and his life ran out...

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Thanks to him, Mt. Tianheng still stands tall and proud to this day. And the blood that he lost in the battle turned into the Bishui River.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Hehehe... Whether you believe the story or not, I'm just happy you're willing to listen to me tell it.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Surely, the reason Lantern Rite exists because people throughout the ages have chosen to come together as friends rather than stay in isolation.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Goodbye. May the flames of wisdom spread to all, and never be extinguished.
